domain: Looks up a BattleEffectLinkedObject by id and, depending on the low two bits of flags, releases its existing child link object (mode 0), always spawns a fresh child (mode 2), or reuses an existing child if present else spawns one (mode 1/3); the child is then mode-configured (SetMode/Func_08009098 per case), tagged with the parent's id, given the template's callback/visual-clear pair, linked back to the parent, and has its visual flags merged from either its own or the parent's visual flags depending on bit 0x100 of flags -- the same two-branch mask/OR merge as the family template, reusing the same 12/13 literal masks and the same struct layout (visual at +0x50, resource-link at +0x68, callback at +0x6c).
notes: The raw candidate-show score is dominated by a single upstream length mismatch: the reference reserves two extra prologue instructions (`movs r5,#0` / `movs r6,#0`, initializing the child pointer and a resource-clear zero before the object==0 test) that no C spelling tried here retains -- every straightforward path (`child = 0;` as an initializer, as a separate first statement, before or after the null check, paired with or without a matching `s32 zero = 0;` for the `object->resource = 0;` write in the release branch) gets eliminated as a provably-dead store, since every reachable path already overwrites `child` before use. A `volatile` qualifier does force the store back but overcorrects (forces stores everywhere else too, regressing to 254 candidate bytes), so it was rejected as not a genuine source-shape fix.

With `--align`, the reference and candidate line up almost instruction-for-instruction for the entire rest of the function once this 4-byte prefix gap is discounted: identical branch structure for the mode==0/2/(1-or-3-with-existing-resource) three-way dispatch (including which sub-case is placed inline vs. out-of-line), identical switch-style case-1/case-2 tail using `beq` chains (not nested if/else with `bne` skips), identical literal masks (13/-13/4, 12) and register roles for the visual-flags merge, and the corrected `child->resource = object` back-reference store (the initial draft had this backwards as `object->resource = child`, which is a genuinely different field write and was the single largest structural bug found and fixed).

Getting the visible field layout right required two real corrections beyond the missing prologue: (1) the child object's mode/setup dispatch is a `switch` on `flags & 3`, not an if/else-if chain -- the two compile to different branch shapes even though semantically identical; (2) the trailing back-reference store is `child->resource = object`, not `object->resource = child` (which is only true inside the mode==1 case, separately).

This is a source-shape gap (the exact C idiom that keeps the two dead-looking prologue stores alive in GCC 2.96's weak liveness analysis), not a scheduling residual -- worth a second pass if a sibling owner in this family is found to need the same two-register early-zero prologue, since that would reveal the triggering idiom.

Recovered only from retained GS1 assembly, the exact-C family template (080937b8) and its already-registered struct/callee types, and the approved compiler. No GS2 evidence or external source was used.
